title: Coherent right-adjoint Ind construction at a regular cardinal
statement: Use the universes, coherent infinity categories, spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the filtered completion and compactness conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability], mapping-space adjunctions of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints], and the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], formed in a universe containing all the Ind categories below. Fix an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$ in the smaller universe. Let $\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$ be the infinity category whose objects are small infinity categories admitting all $\lambda$-small colimits and whose morphisms preserve those colimits. For every such $C$, let $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ spanned by small $\lambda$-filtered colimits of representables. Write $j_C:C\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ for its Yoneda embedding. If $u:C\to D$ is a morphism in $\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$, write $j_D:D\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ for the target Yoneda embedding and let $L_u:\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ be the essentially unique extension of $j_Du$ along $j_C$ preserving small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. Then $L_u$ has a right adjoint $u^*:\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ preserving small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. The assignments $C\mapsto\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ and $u\mapsto u^*$ form a coherent contravariant functor $\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda),\mathrm{op}}_\infty\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, including all higher simplices.

source.place: Definition 10.4, lines 896-899 (the coherent Ind functor into presentable categories and right adjoints preserving filtered colimits). Read online 2026-10-17; no Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ and denote the full inclusion of the given Ind category by $i_C$. Enlarge the ambient universe to contain $\mathcal S$ and these functor categories. Compose the restriction to small categories of the coherent opposite functor $C\mapsto C^{\mathrm{op}}$, $u\mapsto u^{\mathrm{op}}$ of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-opposite-involution] with the internal-Hom functor $\operatorname{Fun}(-,\mathcal S)$, contravariant in its first variable, of the cartesian closed $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$; this gives the coherent presheaf functor $C\mapsto\mathcal P(C)$, $u\mapsto P_u=(-)\circ u^{\mathrm{op}}$, contravariant in $C$. Here taking opposites reverses the simplex order, and the internal-Hom action in the source variable is precomposition. In the internal functor model precomposition sends an $n$-simplex $h:D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S$ to $h\circ(u^{\mathrm{op}}\times1)$. Thus its action retains all coherent transformations. The natural exponential construction supplies this functor as $C$ and $u$ vary, including their higher simplices; the identity and composition comparisons are the ones of this internal-Hom functor.

source.place: Sections 3.1.3–3.1.4 (internal Hom and cartesian compatibility); GHN Definition 9.11 (the presheaf functor)

proof.text:
For $X\in\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ the presheaf Ind criterion says that $X$ takes every $\lambda$-small colimiting cocone in $D$ to a limiting cone of spaces. If $q:K\to C$ has such a colimit $c$, then $u q\to u(c)$ is colimiting because $u$ preserves these colimits. Consequently
$$ (P_uX)(c)=X(u(c))\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(u(q(k)))=\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}(P_uX)(q(k)). $$
The same criterion applied to $C$ shows $P_uX\in\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$. This includes $K=\varnothing$: $u$ preserves the initial object and $X$ takes it to a contractible space. Restricting $P_u$ to the indicated full subcategories therefore defines a coherent functor $R_u:\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ with $i_C R_u=P_u i_D$.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, equivalence of (1) and (3); GHN Definition 10.4

proof.text: Both Ind categories are presentable by the Ind presentability theorem, which also says that $j_D$ preserves $\lambda$-small colimits. Thus $j_Du$ preserves these colimits. Apply the filtered-completion extension theorem with source $C$, target $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ and functor $j_Du$. It supplies precisely the functor $L_u$ in the statement, with $L_uj_C\simeq j_Du$, and its final clause shows that $L_u$ preserves all small colimits. The adjoint functor theorem now supplies a coherent mapping-space right adjoint $T_u$, with unit, counit and triangle identities.

For $c\in C$ and $X\in\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ use fullness of the two Ind inclusions, the Yoneda evaluation equivalence, and the mapping-space adjunction from step 3 to obtain
$$ (i_C T_u X)(c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)}(j_Cc,T_uX)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)}(L_uj_Cc,X)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(j_Du(c),i_DX)\simeq(i_DX)(u(c))=(i_C R_uX)(c). $$
All equivalences here are coherent in $(c,X)$: this is part of the Yoneda evaluation and adjunction statements, and $L_uj_C\simeq j_Du$ is an equivalence of coherent functors. Currying gives an equivalence $i_CT_u\simeq i_CR_u$ of functors to $\mathcal P(C)$. A coherent transformation is an equivalence precisely when it is so at every vertex. Since $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ is full in $\mathcal P(C)$, this equivalence and its inverse lie in that full subcategory, so $T_u\simeq R_u$. Substituting this equivalence into the adjunction identifies $R_u$ as a right adjoint to $L_u$; hence take $u^*=R_u$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.3.1 (Yoneda evaluation), Proposition 5.3.5.13 (restriction as right adjoint); Corollary 5.5.2.9(1)

proof.text:
Let $I$ be any small $\lambda$-filtered infinity category and $X:I\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$ a coherent diagram. For every $c\in C$, the objects $j_Cc$ and $j_Du(c)$ are $\lambda$-compact by the Ind theorem. By the definition of compactness their covariant mapping-space functors send these filtered colimiting cocones to colimiting cocones of spaces. Applying Yoneda evaluation and the formula of step 2, the canonical comparison for $R_u$ is therefore identified, after testing by $j_Cc$, with the chain
$$\operatorname{Map}(j_Cc,\operatorname{colim}_I R_uX)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}(j_Cc,R_uX_i)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}(j_Du(c),X_i)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j_Du(c),\operatorname{colim}_I X)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j_Cc,R_u(\operatorname{colim}_I X)).$$
These are the maps induced by the given cocones, hence prove that the actual comparison $\operatorname{colim}_I R_uX\to R_u(\operatorname{colim}_I X)$ induces an equivalence on every such mapping space. Yoneda evaluation identifies these tests with evaluations of its image under $i_C$ at all $c$. The functor-category equivalence criterion makes that image an equivalence of presheaves, and fullness of $i_C$ makes the comparison itself an equivalence. Thus $u^*$ preserves all small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. This uses only the compactness of the Yoneda objects, not the assertion that every compact object is representable.

source.place: Propositions 5.3.5.3 and 5.3.5.5 (filtered closure and compactness of representables); Proposition 5.1.3.1 (Yoneda evaluation)

proof.text:
Restrict the coherent presheaf functor of step 1 to $\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$ in the source and to the full subcategory $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)\subseteq\mathcal P(C)$ in each value. Step 2 proves precisely the invariance needed for this restriction. For clarity, restricting a diagram to invariant full subcategories keeps every simplex of its transformation data whose object-vertices have been retained: fullness puts all these simplices in the smaller functor categories, and face and degeneracy operators are inherited. In particular the presheaf identity, composition and higher comparison data restrict together. For $C\xrightarrow{u}D\xrightarrow{v}E$, the comparison is the restriction of
$$P_uP_v(X)=(X\circ v^{\mathrm{op}})\circ u^{\mathrm{op}}=X\circ(vu)^{\mathrm{op}}=P_{vu}(X),$$
and the identity is precomposition with $1_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}$. These are the comparisons inside the coherent internal-Hom functor, so their higher compatibilities also restrict; no separate choice of right adjoints is being made on edges. By step 4 its edge values are right adjoints to the specified $L_u$, and step 5 gives their filtered-colimit preservation. This is the required coherent contravariant functor, for the fixed infinite regular $\lambda$, including $\lambda=\omega$.

source.place: Definition 9.11 and Definition 10.4; restriction of the coherent presheaf functor, using HTT Corollary 5.3.5.4
